description: The Knockma Forest Loop in County Galway is a scenic woodland walk that climbs to the summit of Knockma Hill, offering wide views across the surrounding countryside. The trail follows well-made forest paths through mixed woodland, with the ascent leading steadily through trees before opening out near the top to reveal views over the plains of north Galway and towards Connemara on a clear day. Knockma Hill is steeped in legend and history. It is traditionally associated with Queen Maeve of Connacht, who is said to be buried here, and the hill has long been regarded as a place of myth and folklore. Along the walk, visitors will notice small fairy doors at the bases of trees, adding a touch of whimsy and linking to the area’s reputation as a home of the fair folk in Irish tradition. Throughout the forest there are several interesting features, including wooden carvings and ancient stone remains that hint at centuries of settlement and storytelling linked to the hill. These elements give the walk a distinctive blend of natural beauty, local craft, and cultural heritage. The loop eventually circles back through shaded woodland, making it a varied and rewarding route suitable for most walkers. With its mix of folklore, forest charm, and far-reaching views, the Knockma Forest Loop captures the unique character of this part of County Galway.
